text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 10 in history:
1190 - Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa, Holy Roman emperor (1155-90), drowned trying to cross the Saleph River in Cilicia (now in Turkey) while on the Third Crusade to free Jerusalem.
1376 - Wenceslas, eldest son of Holy Roman emperor Charles IV, elected king of the Romans.
1688 - James Francis Edward Stuart, known as The Old Pretender, born the only son of the deposed James II of England.
1793 - The first public zoo, the Jardin des Plantes, opened in Paris.
1819 - Gustave Courbet, painter and leader of the French realist movement, born.
1832 - Nikolaus August Otto, German inventor of the four-stroke internal-combustion engine, born.
1836 - Andre-Marie Ampere, French physicist known for his work on electrodynamics, died. He was the first man to develop measuring techniques for electricity.
1865 - The first performance of Wagner's opera "Tristan and Isolde" took place in Munich, Germany.
1868 - Prince Michael of Serbia was assassinated in Belgrade and was replaced by Milan IV.
1906 - Richard John Seddon, prime minister of New Zealand (1893-1906), died.
1909 - The SOS distress signal was used for the first time by the Cunard liner SS Slavonia, wrecked off the Azores.
1921 - Prince Philip, the Duke of Edinburgh and husband of Queen Elizabeth of England, born as Philippos Schleswig-Holstein Soenderburg-Glucksburg on the Greek island of Corfu.
1922 - Judy Garland, U.S. singer and actress, born as Frances Gumm. She starred in "The Wizard of Oz" in which she sang "Somewhere Over The Rainbow"; she won an Academy Award for her performance.
1923 - Robert Maxwell, Czech-born British media tycoon, born. He died in 1991 after falling overboard from his luxury yacht Lady Ghislaine off the Canary Islands.
1924 - Giacomo Matteotti, Italian Socialist leader, kidnapped and murdered by Fascists.
1934 - Frederick Delius, English composer, died.
1937 - Sir Robert Laird Borden, eighth Canadian prime minister (1911-20), died.
1940 - Italy declared itself at war with France and Britain, effective June 11.
1942 - The Germans destroyed the Czech village of Lidice in retaliation for the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich, protector of Bohemia and Moravia, by Czech resistance fighters.
1943 - Hungarian journalist Laszlo Biro patented his ball-point pen.
1946 - U.S. boxer Jack Johnson, the first black to hold the heavyweight boxing championship of the world, died.
1967 - Spencer Tracy, U.S. actor and Oscar winner for his roles in "Captains Courageous" and "Boys' Town", died.

1967 - The Six-Day War ended with Israel capturing Syrian, Jordanian and Egyptian territories, including East Jerusalem, the West Bank, Gaza Strip and the Sinai peninsula; the Soviet Union broke off diplomatic relations with Israel and threatened sanctions unless Israeli forces stopped their advance towards Damascus.
1971 - The U.S. formally ended its 20-year-old embargo on trade with China.
1990 - Alberto Fujimori, of Japanese ancestry, won Peru's presidential election, defeating Mario Vargas Llosa.
1990 - The Civic Forum movement founded by President Vaclav Havel won Czechoslovakia's first free elections since 1946.
1990 - Bulgaria's former communist party won the country's first free elections in more than four decades.
1996 - Britain and Ireland opened Northern Ireland peace talks; the IRA's political arm Sinn Fein was excluded.
